topics.title: Classification of hydrocarbons and their uses

concepts.learning_objective: Classify hydrocarbons as open-chain saturated, unsaturated, alicyclic or aromatic from structure or formula.
Relate common fuels such as LPG, CNG, LNG and coal gas to their sources.
Identify the structural isomers possible for a given alkane formula.
Predict products of decarboxylation, Wurtz reaction and Kolbe's electrolysis.
Explain physical properties and the substitution, oxidation and aromatisation reactions of alkanes.
Compare the stability of staggered and eclipsed conformations of ethane.
Identify alkenes that show geometrical isomerism and compare properties of cis and trans forms.
Predict products of addition of HBr to unsymmetrical alkenes with and without peroxide.
Deduce the structure of an alkene from its ozonolysis products.
Explain the linear structure of ethyne and the acidic character of terminal alkynes.
Describe preparation of ethyne from calcium carbide and the addition of water to alkynes.

topics.title: Aromatic hydrocarbons: structure, aromaticity and preparation

concepts.learning_objective: Explain the equal bond lengths and stability of benzene using resonance.
Apply the conditions of aromaticity and Huckel's (4n + 2) rule.
Recall laboratory methods of preparing benzene.

topics.title: Reactions of benzene, directive influence and carcinogenicity

concepts.learning_objective: Identify electrophiles and products in electrophilic substitution of benzene.
Predict the directive and activating or deactivating effect of substituents on a benzene ring.
State the origin and harmful effects of carcinogenic polynuclear hydrocarbons.
